userStories.description: CRITICAL: Flaky-test evasion narrative shipped as a durable record. Commit 551e5d63 ('reconfirm US-001 branch-divergence blocker on 4th dispatch') records '1 of 8 consecutive full bun test runs this session showed 1 flaky failure that could not be isolated (unrelated to this story's diff)' and explicitly labels it 'non-blocking', and scripts/cam/patterns.md (new bullet, 'bun test's default reporter and this repo's own printError()...') persists 'Full-suite bun test runs are not perfectly stable: 1 of 8 consecutive runs this session reported 6073 pass / 1 fail'. The branch then proceeded as if the suite were green: no root cause, no fix, and no follow-up issue filed (CAM-0511/CAM-0512 on main are unrelated). Non-determinism in a test is a defect, never a pass rationale; the narrative itself is the finding. Required remedy: identify the non-deterministic test (e.g. bun test --reporter=junit as the bullet itself suggests) and fix the root cause or file and link a blocking issue, and drop the 'not perfectly stable / non-blocking' framing from the durable record.

userStories.title: WARNING: US-004's byte ceiling does not bound the log while it is being written…
userStories.description: WARNING [src/commands/setup.ts:484]: US-004's byte ceiling does not bound the log while it is being written. buildConfigLogCapCommand emits 'cat >> LOG; tail -c N LOG > LOG.tmp && mv LOG.tmp LOG', and tmux pipe-pane keeps the 'cat >>' alive for the entire lifetime of the viewer pane, so the rotate only runs once the pipe closes. During the whole session (the only period the file is actually being fed) the log grows without limit, which is exactly the 'unbounded, unrotated' defect the story exists to close; test/setup-config-log.test.ts only observes the file after the bash subprocess exits, so it cannot see this. Use a streaming construction (a bounded rotate loop, or a size check on each append) rather than a post-hoc trim.

userStories.title: WARNING: The EXIT-trap cleanup races the cap's rotate, so AC8's 'removed on men…
userStories.description: WARNING [src/commands/setup.ts:491]: The EXIT-trap cleanup races the cap's rotate, so AC8's 'removed on menu exit with no residue' can fail. buildConfigLogCleanupCommand runs 'tmux pipe-pane -t $PANE; rm -f $CAM_CONFIG_LOG' and returns immediately, while the piped shell is concurrently finishing 'tail -c N LOG > LOG.tmp && mv LOG.tmp LOG'. If the mv lands after the rm, the log file is recreated after cleanup and survives the menu exit (a LOG.tmp can also be left behind). The two halves are only ever tested in isolation (test/setup-config-log.test.ts:71-137), never composed, so the gate cannot catch it. Sequence the teardown (wait for the pipe to drain, or remove after the rotate) instead of firing both concurrently.

userStories.notes: Closing story: it edits scripts/cam/patterns.md and runs the proofs; it must NOT re-open the five production sites (US-001..US-005 own those). AC11 rewrite rationale (this is the auditor finding from the previous round): the spec's original oracle compared the allowlist entry count against the frozen literal 1, which the frozen-comparand lint rule blocks (patterns.md:932, src/supervisor/prd-oracle-lint.ts hasFrozenIntegerComparand) because a literal rots the moment a later commit edits scripts/check-test-tmpdir.ts on main; the comparand is now re-derived live with `git show main:scripts/check-test-tmpdir.ts | grep -cE ...` INSIDE the same clause as the test, which is the prescribed fix and preserves the exact semantics intended (the branch adds zero allowlist entries; main holds exactly the one inherited entry today, verified 1 = 1 on 2026-08-06). Same-clause placement matters: a derivation token in a different clause does not excuse the comparand (patterns.md:934). AC14 bullet: the attribution must literally read (US-006, CAM-503, 2026-08-06) for the oracle to match, per GOTCHA 9; cite CAM-510 in the bullet's prose body so traceability to this issue is not lost. GOTCHA 12: do not claim test/vendor/check-agent-frontmatter-standalone.test.ts fails today, it passes in the full suite and in isolation (434ms); the proof rests on count equality alone. GOTCHA 10 (measurement hygiene): the two runs cost about 190s combined; run from the repo root with no live cam worker pane writing temp in parallel, and take each count AFTER its run, never before the first. If a count command hangs, the environment is still bloated from before and needs the operator's find/xargs palliative first: that is an environment precondition, never a licence to weaken the criterion. GOTCHA 11: the repo-local scratch root, the helper, the test migration and the gate mechanism belong to CAM-508 and must not be re-asserted or modified here. GOTCHA 1: never rewrite AC12 as after <= before; the fixes deliberately create four permanent fixed-parent entries that do not exist today, so equality after a warm-up run is the correct and strictly stronger form. GOTCHA 4 (CAM-507): no rm -rf in any oracle or command. Because the five tests are repo-local by construction (US-001..US-005), AC12's equality holds structurally rather than depending on each test's own cleanup.

findings.text: US-003's dispatch-terminal cleanup is never wired into production. removeCodexInstructionsFile is exported but the only callers in the whole tree are test/supervisor/codex-instructions-reap.test.ts:75/80/149 (verified by grep over src, test and scripts). The story reads 'be removed at the dispatch terminal, so that the largest leak site ... stops accumulating', and AC6 requires proof that 'AFTER the dispatch terminal ZERO instructions files for that agent survive' -- but in the product the last dispatch's file (up to 200 KB of the user's git diff, CAM-354) stays on disk for the life of the supervisor process and forever after it exits. The AC6 test satisfies the criterion only because the test itself calls the reaper it is supposed to observe, so the assertion verifies rmSync, not the dispatch lifecycle. Wire the removal into the real terminal (worker-dispatch.ts removeWorkerTaskPrompt chokepoint, or a path-returning seam on BackendAdapter). The commit's own patterns.md bullet (scripts/cam/patterns.md:1259) states the wiring is absent and defers it to 'a future story'; per the merit-over-cost rule that deferral is not a rationale, it is the finding.

US-003 is the only one of the five sites with no stale-sibling pruning, so the largest leak site (measured 45,580 files / 1.87 GB) is still unbounded. writeCodexInstructionsFile reaps only inside its own <agent>/<pid> leaf; nothing ever prunes abandoned pid (or agent) siblings under tmpdir()/cam-cli-codex-instructions. US-001 (src/release/ship-pr-tempfile.ts:41-63), US-002 (src/vendor/embedded.ts:96-118) and US-005 (src/supervisor/task-prompt-file.ts:24-52) all prune siblings older than STALE_*_AGE_MS; US-003 does not. Verified empirically by the reviewer (see scripts/cam/review-artifact.txt): after planting a 3-day-old sibling pid directory holding a leftover instructions file and driving a second dispatch, the agent directory still contains ["999999", "72601"] and the stale file survives. Net effect: one leftover <=200 KB file carrying the user's git diff accumulates per (agent, supervisor pid) forever. Growth is slower than before but still unbounded, which is not what the story claims to deliver.

Flaky-test evasion narrative shipped as a durable record. Commit 551e5d63 ('reconfirm US-001 branch-divergence blocker on 4th dispatch') records '1 of 8 consecutive full bun test runs this session showed 1 flaky failure that could not be isolated (unrelated to this story's diff)' and explicitly labels it 'non-blocking', and scripts/cam/patterns.md (new bullet, 'bun test's default reporter and this repo's own printError()...') persists 'Full-suite bun test runs are not perfectly stable: 1 of 8 consecutive runs this session reported 6073 pass / 1 fail'. The branch then proceeded as if the suite were green: no root cause, no fix, and no follow-up issue filed (CAM-0511/CAM-0512 on main are unrelated). Non-determinism in a test is a defect, never a pass rationale; the narrative itself is the finding. Required remedy: identify the non-deterministic test (e.g. bun test --reporter=junit as the bullet itself suggests) and fix the root cause or file and link a blocking issue, and drop the 'not perfectly stable / non-blocking' framing from the durable record.

US-004's byte ceiling does not bound the log while it is being written. buildConfigLogCapCommand emits 'cat >> LOG; tail -c N LOG > LOG.tmp && mv LOG.tmp LOG', and tmux pipe-pane keeps the 'cat >>' alive for the entire lifetime of the viewer pane, so the rotate only runs once the pipe closes. During the whole session (the only period the file is actually being fed) the log grows without limit, which is exactly the 'unbounded, unrotated' defect the story exists to close; test/setup-config-log.test.ts only observes the file after the bash subprocess exits, so it cannot see this. Use a streaming construction (a bounded rotate loop, or a size check on each append) rather than a post-hoc trim.

The EXIT-trap cleanup races the cap's rotate, so AC8's 'removed on menu exit with no residue' can fail. buildConfigLogCleanupCommand runs 'tmux pipe-pane -t $PANE; rm -f $CAM_CONFIG_LOG' and returns immediately, while the piped shell is concurrently finishing 'tail -c N LOG > LOG.tmp && mv LOG.tmp LOG'. If the mv lands after the rm, the log file is recreated after cleanup and survives the menu exit (a LOG.tmp can also be left behind). The two halves are only ever tested in isolation (test/setup-config-log.test.ts:71-137), never composed, so the gate cannot catch it. Sequence the teardown (wait for the pipe to drain, or remove after the rotate) instead of firing both concurrently.

resolveTaskPromptClaudeDirFallback() turns previously pure path computations into filesystem side effects: worker-dispatch.ts:44 (out-log path), worker-dispatch.ts:57 and plan-runner.ts:793 (terminal removal), plan-runner.ts:774 (plan out-log path) now mkdir and prune on every call, including on the removal path that is about to delete a file. It can also now throw (EACCES/ENOSPC) where deriving a path never could. Consider splitting path resolution from directory materialization.

The generated cap command interpolates ${CAM_CONFIG_LOG} unquoted three times ('cat >> ${CAM_CONFIG_LOG}; tail -c N ${CAM_CONFIG_LOG} > ${CAM_CONFIG_LOG}.tmp ...'), so a $TMPDIR containing a space or glob character breaks the redirect. The sibling cleanup command already quotes it correctly; quote it here too (the nested tmux/pipe-pane quoting makes this the fiddly one, so a bash -n composed-script assertion is worth adding alongside).

The reap-all-before-write inside <agent>/<pid> contradicts the same function's stated lifetime requirement ('the file must stay on disk for the whole lifetime of the spawned codex exec process'). A same-agent redispatch from the same supervisor process while a previous codex exec is still alive would delete the live process's instructions file. The worker-pane mutex probably prevents this today, but the invariant is undocumented at this call site; a note (or nesting by uuid instead of reaping) would pin it.

The US-005 prune test covers only the stale-sibling case. Its US-001 sibling (test/release/ship-pr-tempfile.test.ts:70-89) also asserts that a RECENT sibling pid directory, i.e. a concurrent live cam process, survives the prune pass; that is the half that actually guards GOTCHA 8 here, and it is missing.
